Subject: Discovery recap + model-fit next steps (streaming UX concerns)

Hi Emma / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an executable plan: 

Summary of the call (short):
- Use-case: real-time clinician-assist summaries during patient intake (short notes, triage hints).
- Data: de-identified intake transcripts (sample size ~1k turns) and a prompt template you already shared.
- Constraints: sub-100ms token latency for streaming primary suggestions, strict adherence to stop sequences for PHI boundaries, and auditability for any hallucinations.

Model-fit recommendations (initial candidates):
- redwood-llama3-13b-q4f16 (quantized, low-cost baseline) — good throughput, watch stop-sequence handling.
- redwood-mix-deploy-7b-v2 (low-latency variant) — optimistic for token latency but slightly lower factuality on long prompts.
- If you want higher accuracy for edge cases: opt-in to redwood-xxl-70b (non-streamed fallbacks for long-form).

Benchmarks & artifacts I attached: model_benchmarks_summary.pdf (quick perf numbers), prompt_set_medtech.csv (our initial prompt/eval set). Please review the prompt set to ensure it matches your clinician flows.

Streaming / UX concerns we noticed in prior pilots:
- Partial-output coherence: partial chunks can form coherent sentences that later change; for clinician trust we should measure full-turn revision rate. Acceptance criteria suggestion: <=5% major-rewrite rate over 1k turns.
- Stop-sequence adherence: imperative when you mark PHI boundaries — target >=99% single-pass adherence.
- Token latency spikes: 95th percentile token latency target < 50ms; 99th < 120ms for production stream.

Proposed evaluation plan (concrete):
1) Quick microbench: run the prompt_set_medtech.csv through the three candidate model variants (hosted) — 2 business days. Output: latency, coherence, stop-sequence metrics.
2) Streaming sim: simulate clinician streaming sessions (prefixes/continues) and capture rewrite/coherence metrics — 48-hour run, can be executed in Redwood Dedicated pool.
3) Quality review: sample 200 full-turns for human annotation (MedTech annotators + Redwood QA).
4) Canary + rollout: if metrics meet thresholds, run a 1-week canary at 5% traffic with automatic fallback to non-streaming responses on failure.

Ask / next steps:
- Can you confirm security/contact for SOC2/IT procurement? (we'll need their point of contact to share the SOC2 report and deployment checklist).
- Are you comfortable with the proposed timing (microbench this week, streaming sim next week)?
- Any additions to the prompt set we should include before we run the microbench?

If you confirm, I'll loop in Vanessa to stand up the Dedicated pool and Grace to run the eval harness.

Thanks —

Markus Klein
